 Persija vs Persik Kediri Final Score 3-1: Rizky Ridho Leads Macan Kemayoran Comeback, Ivan Mamut Scores Final Goal
 Persija Jakarta successfully turned the tide against Persik Kediri in the seventh week of the 2026/2027 BRI Super League, with second-half goals from Denis Kolinger, Rizky Ridho, and Ivan Mamut securing a 3-1 victory.
 By: Damar Prasetya 
 | 
 Editor: Nayla Savitri 
 | 
 Contributor: Niken Pramudya 
 October 26, 2026, 22:10 WITA · 5 min read 
 Image Caption: Illustration of the Persija Jakarta vs Persik Kediri match result with a score of 3-1 in the 2026/2027 BRI Super League, Monday (26/10/2026). (Illustration: Aktualita Sport/) 
 JAKARTA, Aktualita.co - Persija Jakarta successfully turned the tide against Persik Kediri in the seventh week of the 2026/2027 BRI Super League at the Jakarta International Stadium (JIS) on Monday (26/10/2026) evening. 
 The Macan Kemayoran initially trailed after a 10th-minute goal by Imanol Garcia. However, Persija rallied in the second half with goals from Denis Kolinger and Rizky Ridho, before Ivan Mamut extended the lead during injury time. 
 Advertisement 
 According to detikSport match statistics, the game ended with a 3-1 victory for Persija Jakarta . This result adds three crucial points for the team coached by Shin Tae-yong in the race at the top of the standings. 
 This victory was not easily achieved. Persik Kediri provided resistance from the start and managed to maintain their lead throughout the first half. 
 Persija only found their momentum for a comeback after making several player changes following the break. 
 Persik Kediri Takes Early Lead Through Imanol Garcia 
 The match began with both teams trying to develop their play. Persija, appearing in front of their home supporters, tried to build attacks, while Persik did not hesitate to seek opportunities through set-piece situations. 
 A surprise occurred in the 10th minute when the visitors opened the scoring through Imanol Garcia. 
 The goal originated from an Ernesto Gomez corner kick. The ball, directed into the Persija defensive area, was met by Garcia with a header that goalkeeper Nadeo Argawinata could not anticipate. 
 Persik led 1-0, forcing Persija to chase the deficit. 
 This lead became a valuable asset for Marcos Reina's side. Persik attempted to maintain their defensive organization while hindering the hosts' efforts to create chances. 
 Persija made a change in the defensive sector by bringing on Rio Fahmi to replace Kerim Memija in the first half. 
 However, until the referee blew the whistle to end the first half, Persija was unable to score an equalizer. 
 The 0-1 score for Persik Kediri held until halftime. 
 Denis Kolinger and Rizky Ridho Turn the Tide 
 Entering the second half, Shin Tae-yong made important changes to improve the balance of the game. 
 Rizky Ridho, who started the match on the bench, came on to replace Fabio Calonego. Kwon Chang-hoon also received playing time, replacing Witan Sulaeman. 
 Ridho's presence provided additional strength for Persija as they sought to overcome the deficit. 
 After several attempts to build attacks, Persija finally managed to equalize through Denis Kolinger around the 64th minute. 
 The Croatian defender capitalized on an opportunity from a Rayhan Hannan pass to make the score 1-1. 
 Kolinger's goal became the turning point of the match. Persija, who previously struggled to penetrate the opponent's defense, gained momentum to increase the pressure. 
 Not long after the equalizer, Rizky Ridho made the home crowd cheer again. 
 The Indonesian national team defender successfully capitalized on a set-piece situation involving Denis Kolinger. Ridho unleashed a direct finish to put Persija ahead 2-1. 
 Two goals in quick succession changed the course of the match. 
 Persik, who previously led, had to change their approach to seek an equalizer, while Persija tried to maintain their lead. 
 Ivan Mamut Adds Goal in Injury Time 
 Persija did not fully ease off the attack after turning the situation around. 
 Entering the final minutes of the match, Shin Tae-yong made another substitution to refresh the front line. 
 Ivan Mamut came on to replace Alexander Jeremejeff toward the end of normal time. 
 The decision paid off when Mamut was credited with a goal in the 90+5 minute according to detikSport match statistics. 
 The goal gave Persija a 3-1 lead and widened the gap from Persik Kediri at the end of the match. 
 For Persija, the additional goal in injury time capped off their struggle after trailing throughout the first half. 
 Meanwhile, Persik had to accept a disappointing result after failing to maintain the lead they held from the early minutes. 
 Persija vs Persik Kediri Statistics 
 DetikSport statistics show Persija was slightly superior in ball possession and the number of chances created. 
 Persija controlled 56 percent of possession, while Persik recorded 44 percent. 
 In terms of attack, the hosts recorded eight shots with five on target. Persik produced seven shots, including four on target. 
 Persija also recorded a passing accuracy of 74 percent, higher than Persik, which was at 69 percent. 
 Both teams earned four corner kicks each. 
 These statistics show the match was quite competitive, although Persija was able to maximize key opportunities in the second half. 
 Persija Strengthens Position at the Top of the Standings 
 The victory over Persik is the second consecutive positive result for Persija after previously crushing Arema FC 5-1 on October 21, 2026. 
 Before facing Persik, the Macan Kemayoran led the standings with 15 points from six matches. 
 The additional three points bring Persija to 18 points from seven matches, with a record of six wins and one loss. 
 Conversely, Persik Kediri remains stuck with 10 points after seven matches. 
 This result also extends Persija's positive record in meetings against Persik. 
 In the two previous meetings, Persija also won 3-1, namely in November 2025 and May 2026. 
 Shin Tae-yong Had Warned of Persik's Strength 
 Before the match took place, Shin Tae-yong had warned Persija players about the quality of Persik Kediri. 
 The South Korean coach assessed that Persik is an opponent with a fairly solid organizational play, requiring the right tactical approach. 
 "The match was not easy. However, we prepared tactics to beat the opponent," said Shin Tae-yong in his statement ahead of the match.
 Shin's warning proved relevant when Persija had to face an early deficit. 
 However, the changes made in the second half successfully changed the situation of the match. 
 Persija is next scheduled to face Dewa United Banten FC on October 31, 2026. 
 That match will be the next test for the Macan Kemayoran to maintain consistency while keeping their position in the 2026/2027 BRI Super League title race.
